name: Vancouver
operatingHours: SkyTrain (Expo, Millennium and Canada lines) runs ~5:00 AM–1:15 AM Mon–Fri, ~6:00 AM–1:15 AM Sat and ~7:00 AM–12:15 AM Sun/holidays; trains every 2–6 min by day, 6–10 min late evening. NightBus routes cover the overnight gap.
fareInfo: From 1 July 2026 a one-zone adult fare is C$2.85 by Compass card or tap-to-pay (contactless card/phone) and C$3.50 cash; SkyTrain uses 1–3 zones on weekdays until 6:30 PM and one zone on evenings/weekends, with 90-minute transfers. Journeys starting at the YVR SkyTrain stations add a C$6.50 AddFare (~C$11 total to downtown). A Compass DayPass is ~C$12.

sights.name: Stanley Park
sights.note: A 400-hectare rainforest peninsula beside downtown, ringed by the seawall and dotted with beaches, lagoons and old-growth cedars.

sights.name: Granville Island Public Market
sights.note: The covered food hall at the heart of Granville Island's artist studios and docks, reached by tiny Aquabus ferries from downtown.

sights.name: Vancouver Aquarium
sights.note: Canada's largest aquarium, inside Stanley Park, with sea otters, Pacific coast habitats and a rescued-marine-mammal focus.

sights.name: Gastown Steam Clock
sights.note: A steam-powered clock that whistles every quarter-hour on the cobbled main street of Gastown, the city's oldest quarter.

sights.name: Museum of Anthropology at UBC
sights.note: A glass-walled Arthur Erickson building holding monumental Northwest Coast totem poles and Bill Reid's carvings, on the UBC campus.
sights.hours: Daily 10:00 AM–5:00 PM, Thu to 9:00 PM; closed Mon mid-Oct–mid-May

sights.name: Canada Place
sights.note: The sail-roofed cruise terminal on the harbour, with a free waterfront promenade looking to the North Shore mountains and FlyOver Canada inside.
sights.hours: Promenade open 24 hours; FlyOver Canada ~10:00 AM–9:00 PM

sights.name: VanDusen Botanical Garden
sights.note: A 22-hectare garden of lakes, a hedge maze and plants from every continent, with a winter Festival of Lights.
sights.hours: Daily ~10:00 AM–4:00 PM in winter, to ~7:00 PM in summer

sights.name: Vancouver Seawall
sights.note: A 28 km waterfront path for walking and cycling that loops Stanley Park and runs on to English Bay, False Creek and Kitsilano.
sights.hours: Open 24 hours (separate bike and foot lanes)

sights.name: Queen Elizabeth Park & Bloedel Conservatory
sights.note: The city's highest point, with quarry gardens, skyline views and a domed tropical conservatory full of free-flying birds.
sights.hours: Park 24 hours; conservatory daily ~10:00 AM–5:00 PM

sights.name: Science World
sights.note: A hands-on science centre inside the geodesic dome at the end of False Creek, steps from Main Street SkyTrain.
sights.hours: Daily 10:00 AM–5:00 PM (to 6:00 PM in summer)

sights.name: Kitsilano Beach
sights.note: A lively sandy beach with volleyball courts, a long saltwater pool in summer and views back to downtown.

sights.name: English Bay Beach
sights.note: The West End's city beach, known for its sunsets, the laughing-men sculptures and summer fireworks.

sights.name: Vancouver Public Library, Central Library
sights.note: A Colosseum-like library building with a free rooftop garden offering views over downtown.
sights.hours: ~10:00 AM–8:00 PM Mon–Thu, shorter hours Fri–Sun; rooftop garden seasonal

sights.name: Brockton Point Totem Poles
sights.note: A cluster of carved First Nations totem poles on the Stanley Park seawall, the province's most visited outdoor landmark.

sights.name: The Marine Building
sights.note: A 1930 Art Deco tower whose lobby is a riot of brass, sea creatures and stained glass.

sights.name: Dr. Sun Yat-Sen Classical Chinese Garden
sights.note: A Ming-style scholar's garden of pavilions, jade-green ponds and rockery in Chinatown, with a free public park next door.
sights.hours: ~10:00 AM–4:30 PM in winter, longer in summer

sights.name: Spanish Banks
sights.note: A long, quiet tidal beach west of Kitsilano with free sunset views across English Bay to downtown and the North Shore mountains.

railStations.name: Pacific Central Station
railStations.note: Vancouver's intercity station: VIA Rail's Canadian to Jasper and Toronto, Amtrak Cascades to Seattle and Portland, plus intercity coaches. Main Street–Science World SkyTrain (Expo Line) is a 3-minute walk across Thornton Park.
railStations.hours: Station opens ~6:00 AM–9:30 PM around departures; Amtrak ~2 trains/day, VIA ~2–3 trains/week.

airports.name: Vancouver International Airport
airports.transitNote: The Canada Line (on the SkyTrain map) runs from YVR–Airport station, between the domestic and international terminals, to Waterfront downtown in ~25 min, every ~6–8 min; single fares pay a C$6.50 AddFare (~C$11). Taxis use flat-rate zones (~C$35–45 downtown, ~25 min).
airports.hours: Canada Line: first train ~5:00 AM (later on Sun), last ~1:00 AM. Late arrivals: taxi/rideshare or the N10 night bus.
